R2-01.why: The fantasy (wreck the house, hide it before Mom gets home) makes sense to a child at once, and kids only need a thumbstick and one contextual button. But the round switches rules three times (party, panic, hunt), and the Parent has 3 gadgets plus a FREEZE timing rule, so a first-time Parent or a first PANIC phase will confuse kids.
R2-01.fix: Open each phase with a full-screen pictogram of its single goal, such as 'HIDE!' with an arrow to the nearest glowing mess. Give a first-time Parent a single Sniff gadget and add the other gadgets with mastery.

R2-02.why: One HOLD button with no thumbstick is about as simple as controls get, and the chaos of spinning off course is fun even when you fail. But kids won't work out in seconds that their seat pushes the raft in one direction, so early runs can feel random ('why are we spinning?').
R2-02.fix: Show a live raft-heading arrow that combines everyone's input, with a ghost arrow for 'paddle now'. Start every new player with a 2-seat tandem stretch of calm water before the rapids.

R2-03.why: Red Light Green Light is familiar and 'let go of the stick to freeze' is easy to grasp. But the extra rules pile up: freeze on your plinth, match your pose placard, NPC statues that shift, the Guard's battery, and penalties for wrong tags. Those are hard for 8-10 year olds to infer without explanation.
R2-03.fix: Drop the off-plinth rule, or make it automatic by snapping a frozen statue into the nearest plinth pose. Put a large 'LIGHT COMING' vignette on statue screens so kids know when to freeze without having to read the Guard.

R2-04.why: With no movement or camera control and the whole screen as a drawing pad, there is very little to manage. Kids can already draw hearts, circles and zigzags, the first runs show trace guides, and a sloppy shape still casts something, so a child gets a satisfying 'draw, then boom' within seconds. The drawbacks are memorising which rune does what, the 1-second fusion timing, and reading the relic drafts.
R2-04.fix: Keep a small row of rune icons with their effect pictures on screen at all times. Make relic drafts icon-only (no text) and auto-pick after 5 s.

R2-05.why: Social deduction, a different inspection tool per player, back-room swaps, vouching, an evidence board and voting meetings stack several abstract systems on top of each other. Deliberate deceit and working out 'who touched what' from icons is a lot of thinking for 8-10 year olds, and the goal ('catch the forger while running a shop') can't be read in 10 seconds even with pictures.
R2-05.fix: Make the PvE 'Open Shop' mode the default first-session experience: one tool, a glowing tell, then BUY or REJECT. Unlock forger roles only after 3 rounds, and give forgers one scripted 'swap' prompt.

R2-06.why: Patrollers have an easy job (follow the arrow, tap the anomaly), but spotting anomalies means remembering what 'normal' looks like across a grid of cameras, which is hard for young players. The Watcher role carries most of the thinking, and the chase horror in a haunted motel may put off younger kids.
R2-06.fix: Have the Watcher's feed show a flashing 'something changed!' highlight with a before/after flicker on the first nights. Add a lighter 'silly anomalies' tier for new players.

R2-07.why: 'Film the ghosts' plus a VIEWS counter and generous auto-framing is clear for whoever holds the camera. The pitch doesn't say what the other players do or which controls they use, and the 6-minute expedition has no step-by-step goals beyond the daily contracts.
R2-07.fix: Give every role a visible job, for example a lure-holder who draws ghosts toward the camera. Pin the current goal as an icon at the top of the screen ('film ghost stealing hat').

R2-08.why: 'Carry the cake to the door without bumping it' needs no tutorial: the floating value meter and the physical reactions (cake sags, aquarium sloshes, dragon stirs) teach each rule visually, and grabbing is automatic. Linked two-person carries and the many hazards add some complexity, and the mobile layout isn't specified.
R2-08.fix: Show a ghost trail or arrow to the delivery door, and add a 1-second pictogram pop-up the first time each parcel type is picked up ('no running!' icon). Specify the mobile layout as thumbstick plus one GRAB/DROP button.

R2-09.why: Drag-and-tap with an AUTO-PLACE option is easy to physically operate, and creatures appeal to kids. But auto-battler outcomes are opaque, so kids won't know why they lost. Board placement, signature timing, knockouts, gremlin hazards, hearts, trait inheritance and mutations add up to a heavy pile of systems for a 4-minute match.
R2-09.fix: Show a large green/red 'tap NOW' ring for the signature move and replay the decisive moment after each fight. Hide breeding until after the first few matches.

R2-10.why: A pictographic manual and matching stamps remove the need to read, and failure is gentle and funny. But following symbol-to-colour-to-action rules and relaying them without chat under a 60-90 s timer is a heavy working-memory task for 8-10 year olds, and the person holding the Book has no intuitive verb.
R2-10.fix: Begin with one-step modules (symbol to action, no colour) and no timer. Have tapping a manual symbol auto-highlight the matching part on the partner's device so relaying becomes a single tap.

R2-11.why: Flashing icons over stations, plus 'run there and fix it', is the Overcooked formula that kids pick up immediately. But it's unclear whether players must fetch tools, cascading failures can overwhelm young players, and rotating roles (pilot yoke vs runner) changes the controls partway through.
R2-11.fix: Make every station a one-button 'hold to fix' with no tool fetching. Cap simultaneous emergencies to 2 on the easiest route, and show a role card ('You are PILOT: drag to steer') for 2 s at each rotation.

R2-12.why: Fire means spray it and a trapped animal means save it, so the goals are universal and visual, and the controls are a thumbstick, auto-aimed HOLD SPRAY and a single RESCUE button. Smoke hiding rooms and finding the ambulance on a procedural layout may disorient young players, and the special two-player and tool rescues need a little teaching.
R2-12.fix: Have each critter call out with an on-screen paw marker through the smoke. After pickup, show a glowing path to the ambulance, and make tool rescues show the needed tool icon above the critter.

overall_notes: The strongest concepts for young players combine a goal a child already understands (fire/animals, fragile cake, draw a shape) with one or two buttons and auto-aim or auto-grab: R2-04, R2-08 and R2-12. The weakest stack abstract systems such as deception, memory of what 'normal' looks like, rule chains or auto-battler opacity: R2-05, R2-06, R2-09 and R2-10. A frequent gap is a missing 'where do I go' guide (arrow or trail) and text-heavy steps (relic drafts, role changes) that should be icons. Asymmetric games score the more complex role low; the easy role doesn't carry it.
